title: Everything you need to know about Dragon Ball, ahead of a rumoured LEGO theme
summary: With whispers of a LEGO Dragon Ball theme growing louder, here's a quick primer on the franchise for fans who only know it from memes and pop culture.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics has put together a beginner's guide to Dragon Ball for LEGO fans, timed around ongoing **rumours** (not yet confirmed) of a LEGO Dragon Ball theme.

According to these rumours, the theme could kick off with an 11390 Shenron set under LEGO Icons as early as November, followed by a broader wave of sets in April 2027. The rumoured 2027 line-up reportedly includes models such as Goku vs Raditz, Arrival on Namek, Z Fighters vs Saiyans, Porunga and the Final Battle, Frieza's Spaceship, Kame House, a buildable Vegeta figure, and at least one polybag, alongside another set yet to be named. Prices and piece counts for these are all still unconfirmed.

For context, Dragon Ball is a long-running Japanese media franchise created by Akira Toriyama, starting as a manga in 1984 before spawning multiple anime series, games, merchandise, and even a theme park planned for Qiddiya City in Saudi Arabia. Its visual style is generally simpler than many other anime, which the article suggests could make it a good fit for LEGO building, pointing to Shenron's rounded, dome-like shapes and the iconic pink Kame House as relatively achievable in brick form.

Brick Fanatics also notes that this rumoured release pattern echoes the structure already **confirmed** for LEGO KPop Demon Hunters, though it stresses that Dragon Ball itself remains firmly in rumour territory for now.

## Why it matters
If a LEGO Dragon Ball theme does materialise, it would mark another major anime licence joining the LEGO catalogue, likely appealing to collectors, display builders and anyone hunting the next big crossover set. Getting familiar with the source material now means UK fans can spot standout builds and hidden details early if the rumours turn into official sets.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for any official LEGO announcement confirming (or denying) 11390 Shenron and the wider rumoured 2027 wave, plus firm pricing, piece counts and UK release dates once these move beyond rumour stage.

The orb uses a complex weave of cables, gold elements and flame pieces to create concave geometry that reacts strikingly to both natural and blacklight lighting.

This isn't Baum's first foray into this style: the sphere follows an earlier eyeball MOC built using similar 'brickbending' techniques, where standard LEGO elements are combined in unconventional ways to create smooth, curved forms rather than the blocky shapes bricks are typically known for.

title: LEGO reveals 931-piece Ayrton Senna Helmet set
summary: LEGO Editions has officially unveiled 43024 Ayrton Senna Helmet, its biggest F1 helmet build yet, complete with a new Senna minifigure.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO has officially revealed 43024 Ayrton Senna Helmet, the newest addition to its LEGO Editions range celebrating notable sporting and musical figures. At 931 pieces, it's now the largest Formula 1 helmet set in the collection, beating out the previous Ferrari-themed Leclerc and Hamilton helmet builds.

The set recreates the design Senna wore during his dominant 1988 championship-winning season, featuring the green, yellow and blue of the Brazilian flag along with the red and white scheme from his original helmet - though the Marlboro branding has been left out. A plaque commemorates his 1988 title, complete with his name, signature and logo.

It also includes a brand new Senna minifigure, distinct from the one bundled with 2024's 10330 McLaren MP4/4 & Ayrton Senna, sporting fully red legs, dual-moulded arms and a torso printed with a Senninha t-shirt design.

The finished model stands 19cm tall and will retail at £79.99 / $89.99 / €89.99 when it launches on 1 September 2026.

## Why it matters
This is the first LEGO Editions helmet to step outside the current Formula 1 driver line-up, opening the door for more legacy or historic driver sets in future. For F1 fans and LEGO collectors, it's also a chance to grab a fresh Senna minifigure with a different design to the one already out there.

## What to watch next

title: LEGO Ideas designer looks back on 10-year journey to The X-Files set
summary: With LEGO Ideas 21369 The X-Files now on shelves, fan designer Brent Waller has shared the decade-long story behind the set, from a 2014 hobby build to a hit release causing stock shortages.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO Ideas 21369 The X-Files has officially launched, and to mark the occasion, fan designer Brent Waller has spoken about the long road to get it made.

According to an interview shared via LEGO Ideas, Waller first built a version of Mulder's cluttered office back in 2014, purely for his own collection, inspired by watching the show's original 1993 TV advert. LEGO Ideas wasn't accepting that kind of submission at the time, so he posted photos on Flickr instead.

Those photos reportedly caught the attention of actor Gillian Anderson, who played Scully, and her assistant asked Waller for a copy of the minifigures. Anderson happily posed with them, helping spark fan interest in an official set.

Waller resubmitted a revised design on LEGO Ideas five years later. It hit 10,000 supporters but wasn't approved that time. The project finally found its moment when LEGO Ideas launched a '90s-themed challenge, giving Waller the chance to rework the concept - this time shifting focus to the show's atmospheric Pacific Northwest forest setting rather than just the office.

The finished 21369 The X-Files set is now available, and by all accounts it's proving popular, with reports of stock shortages and fans creating their own remixes and MOCs based on it.

## Why it matters
Stories like this show just how long-term and personal the LEGO Ideas process can be for fan designers, sometimes spanning a decade before a concept becomes an official set. It's also a nice reminder for UK builders and collectors that popular Ideas sets can sell out fast, so acting quickly matters if you want one at retail price.

## What to watch next
Worth keeping an eye on secondary market prices and restock updates for 21369 The X-Files given the reported shortages, plus any further fan remixes or MOCs inspired by Waller's design.

bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics has reviewed 76476 The Ministry of Magic Collectors' Edition, the latest large-scale LEGO Harry Potter set, giving it an overall score of 4/10. The set follows on from the well-received Burrow and Hogsmeade Collectors' Edition sets, but the reviewer says this one struggles across the board.

According to the review, the design splits the Ministry of Magic across multiple underground levels beneath a London street scene, echoing the layered approach used in the Gringotts Wizarding Bank Collectors' Edition set. It covers familiar Order of the Phoenix locations including the Hall of Prophecy, the Death Chamber, the Wizengamot courtroom, and the offices of Umbridge and Arthur Weasley.

The breakdown scores given were Design 3/10, Playability 2/10, Value 5/10, Minifigures 6/10, and Build 6/10. Positives highlighted include the London street level and some new printed pieces, while criticisms focus on an overly ambitious concept, visible cost-cutting on minifigures, and pricing that the reviewer feels doesn't match what's on offer.
